scenarios.title: Security & defence analysis
scenarios.goal: Continuously review logs, threat-intel feeds, and vulnerability reports to surface risks, correlate indicators, and produce actionable briefings without giving the agent blanket access to production systems.
setup: Agent is scoped to read-only log directories or SIEM export buckets inside the sandbox.
Threat-intel feeds are fetched via signed, public APIs or locally mirrored datasets.
Vulnerability scans are imported as files or via a read-only API token with no write permissions.
workflow: Ingest the last 24 hours of firewall, endpoint, and authentication logs.
Extract IPs, hashes, and domains and cross-reference them against threat-intel feeds.
Cluster related events into potential incidents and score each by severity.
Draft a briefing with IOCs, affected assets, and recommended next steps.
Queue the briefing for analyst review.

humanApproved: Block an IP or isolate a host

safeguards: All file system and network access is confined to the Linux sandbox.
Write access to security tools is disabled; the agent cannot modify firewall or EDR rules.
Sensitive log paths are explicitly allow-listed rather than granting home-directory access.
Output is marked as a draft until a human analyst approves it.
outcomes: Reduce mean time to triage by 40–60% for routine alert queues.
Standardize briefing format across shifts.
Catch low-signal correlations that manual review often misses.

scenarios.title: Incident response
scenarios.goal: Accelerate containment and communication during a security or operational incident by automating evidence collection and runbook drafting while keeping containment actions behind explicit human approval.
setup: Incident channel or ticket system is accessible via a read-only API or webhook.
Runbook templates are stored as project memory.
Sandbox has network access only to internal observability endpoints, not customer data stores.
workflow: Receive incident trigger from monitoring webhook or ticket label.
Collect recent logs, metrics, and deployment events around the affected window.
Identify likely root causes and affected services from the evidence.
Draft a timeline and a containment runbook with rollback options.
Notify the on-call engineer and present one-click approval actions.
safeguards: Containment tools are gated behind per-tool approval toggles.
All commands run inside the sandbox first; destructive commands require explicit confirmation.
Customer-facing messages must be reviewed before sending.
Audit trail of every command and decision is written to project memory.
outcomes: Cut initial evidence-gathering time from tens of minutes to under two minutes.
Reduce miscommunication during handoffs with a consistent incident timeline.
Maintain an auditable record for post-incident reviews.

scenarios.title: Management reporting
scenarios.goal: Turn scattered project signals into concise, decision-ready reports for leadership, automating data gathering and narrative drafting while leaving publication and interpretation to humans.
setup: Read-only access to project trackers, code repositories, and CI/CD dashboards.
Report template and KPI definitions stored in project memory.
Optional connection to a spreadsheet or BI tool via a user-supplied API key.
workflow: Query tickets, pull requests, CI runs, and release notes for the reporting period.
Calculate velocity, defect rates, deployment frequency, and open risks.
Generate charts and a plain-language narrative with highlights and caveats.
Format the report into the chosen template.
Present the draft to the report owner for review and distribution.
safeguards: Data sources are read-only; the agent cannot create or delete records.
Aggregated metrics are preferred over individual employee surveillance.
Draft language includes confidence labels and data-source footnotes.
No report leaves the local environment until a human approves it.
outcomes: Reduce report-assembly time from hours to minutes.
Improve consistency of KPI definitions across teams.
Free managers to focus on interpretation instead of spreadsheet wrangling.

scenarios.title: Marketing operations
scenarios.goal: Draft, localize, and schedule campaign content across channels while keeping every public publish action behind human approval and avoiding claims of built-in platform access.
setup: Brand voice, audience segments, and campaign calendar stored in project memory.
User provides API keys or export credentials for each marketing platform locally.
Asset library is mounted read-only inside the sandbox.
workflow: Read campaign brief and target audience from project memory.
Draft copy variants, subject lines, and social snippets.
Localize content for each region using approved terminology glossaries.
Generate a scheduling proposal aligned with the campaign calendar.
Queue drafts for marketer review and one-click publish/schedule.
safeguards: Platform credentials are stored in local runtime storage, never in the repository or build artifacts.
Publish actions require explicit confirmation and are logged.
Generated claims are flagged for fact-checking before approval.
Tone and compliance checks run against a stored brand policy.
outcomes: Reduce time to first draft by 50–70%.
Improve brand consistency across channels.
Catch scheduling conflicts before content goes live.

scenarios.title: Daily assistance
scenarios.goal: Help a knowledge worker summarize meetings, manage notes, draft routine messages, and surface reminders without accessing private accounts the user has not explicitly connected.
setup: User selects which local files, calendars, or note exports the agent may read.
Sandbox is limited to an isolated workspace folder, not the full home directory.
Any outbound sending uses a user-supplied mail or chat bridge configured locally.
workflow: Read exported meeting transcripts and notes from the workspace folder.
Extract action items, decisions, and open questions.
Draft follow-up messages and calendar holds.
Suggest prioritization based on deadlines and participants.
Present drafts for user approval before sending or creating events.
safeguards: The agent only reads files the user has copied into the workspace.
No cloud account credentials are requested unless the user opts in.
Drafts are surfaced in the UI, not sent automatically.
Sensitive content can be excluded via filename or folder patterns.
outcomes: Recover 30–60 minutes per day on note-taking and follow-ups.
Reduce missed action items from meetings.
Keep personal data inside the local sandbox.

scenarios.title: Browser research
scenarios.goal: Conduct structured web research, synthesize multiple sources, and produce cited summaries while avoiding unauthorized data collection and clearly separating autonomous browsing from human decisions.
setup: User defines search queries, trusted source allow-lists, and depth limits.
Browser tool or MCP server runs inside the sandbox with no access to the host browser profile.
Ad-block and rate-limit policies are enforced at the sandbox network layer.
workflow: Run targeted searches against public search engines or APIs.
Fetch pages from the allow-listed domains.
Extract claims, quotes, and citations into a structured note.
Cross-check facts across sources and flag contradictions.
Produce a sourced summary with confidence labels.
safeguards: Only public, allow-listed sites are reachable.
Rate limits prevent aggressive crawling.
Personal browser sessions and cookies stay outside the sandbox.
All citations are preserved so humans can verify claims.
outcomes: Reduce research time by 50% for literature and competitive reviews.
Improve citation traceability.
Surface contradictions between sources early.

scenarios.title: WhatsApp communication
scenarios.goal: Assist with WhatsApp-based support, coordination, or outreach by reading and drafting messages through a user-controlled local bridge, with sending always requiring explicit approval.
setup: User installs and runs a local WhatsApp Web bridge or official Business API client in the sandbox.
Authentication is performed by the user via QR code or token; OWLLM never stores WhatsApp credentials.
Only approved chat identifiers are reachable; broadcast lists are disabled by default.
workflow: Poll the local bridge for incoming messages within the approved scope.
Classify messages by intent and urgency.
Draft replies using project memory templates.
Surface high-priority threads to the user.
Send only after the user clicks approve for each message.
safeguards: OWLLM has no native WhatsApp integration; all access flows through a user-managed bridge.
Outgoing messages require per-message or per-thread approval.
No message content is retained beyond what the user configures in project memory.
Blocklist prevents replies to unknown or unauthorized contacts.
outcomes: Cut response latency for routine support questions.
Maintain a human-in-the-loop for all outbound communication.
Keep WhatsApp credentials outside the application repository.

scenarios.title: Email triage
scenarios.goal: Reduce email overload by categorizing messages, drafting replies, and surfacing urgent threads while treating the mailbox as a user-connected service that OWLLM does not natively host.
setup: User provides IMAP/SMTP credentials or app-passwords through local runtime storage.
Mailbox access is read-only by default; send permission is granted per draft.
Folder allow-lists and sender blocklists are configured up front.
workflow: Connect to the user's mail server over TLS.
Categorize unread mail by urgency, sender, and topic.
Draft contextual replies for routine categories.
Flag messages that need immediate human attention.
Queue approved drafts for sending via SMTP.
safeguards: Credentials are never committed or bundled in builds.
The agent cannot delete, forward, or move messages without explicit permission.
Drafts include a clear indication that they were generated.
All send actions are logged and require user confirmation.
outcomes: Reduce inbox review time by 30–50%.
Speed up replies to routine inquiries.
Lower the risk of missing critical emails in high-volume periods.

scenarios.title: CRM maintenance
scenarios.goal: Keep customer records clean and up to date by reading CRM data, flagging duplicates and gaps, and proposing updates that a human approves before writing back.
setup: User supplies a read-only or scoped CRM API key through local runtime storage.
Record types and fields the agent may inspect are explicitly allow-listed.
Write operations are disabled until the user enables them per-session.
workflow: Pull records for the configured objects and date range.
Detect duplicates using fuzzy matching on name, email, and company.
Flag missing or stale fields against validation rules.
Propose merges, updates, and enrichment sources.
Present a human-approved change list for review and apply only selected items.
safeguards: API scope is read-only by default.
Write actions are batched and require explicit approval.
A dry-run preview shows exactly what would change.
All changes are logged with before/after values.
outcomes: Improve CRM data quality without risky bulk automation.
Reduce manual duplicate cleanup by 60%.
Give sales teams confidence that records stay accurate.

scenarios.title: Multi-agent software delivery
scenarios.goal: Deliver software features using a team of specialized agents for planning, coding, review, and testing, with final commit, merge, and deployment decisions reserved for humans.
setup: Project is opened in a Code page with per-project persistence.
Agents operate in the Linux sandbox with access only to the project working directory.
Repository remotes are configured by the user; the agent does not hold Git credentials.
workflow: Planner agent breaks the feature into tasks and acceptance criteria.
Coder agent implements changes in the sandboxed working directory.
Reviewer agent checks style, tests, and security patterns.
Tester agent runs the test suite and reports failures.
Human lead reviews the diff, approves, and commits or merges.
safeguards: All code changes are confined to the sandbox and visible in the working directory.
Tests must pass before the human is prompted to commit.
Git credentials remain under user control; the agent cannot push without approval.
Destructive commands require explicit confirmation and are audited.
outcomes: Accelerate feature prototyping by 2–3x for well-scoped tasks.
Keep a tight review loop so quality does not degrade.
Preserve developer accountability for every commit and release.
